<rules>

<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

% Adjacent moves (4‑connected neighbourhood)
adj(0,1).
adj(0,-1).
adj(1,0).
adj(-1,0).

% ---- Cells that are outside colour 5 (cannot be reached from the border without crossing a 5) ----
boundary5(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 5, R = 0.
boundary5(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 5, R = #count{R2 : input(R2,_,_)} - 1.
boundary5(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 5, C = 0.
boundary5(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 5, C = #count{C2 : input(_,C2,_)} - 1.

outside5(R,C) :- boundary5(R,C).
outside5(R2,C2) :- outside5(R1,C1), adj(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC, input(R2,C2,V), V != 5.

% ---- Cells that are outside colour 2 ----
boundary2(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 2, R = 0.
boundary2(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 2, R = #count{R2 : input(R2,_,_)} - 1.
boundary2(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 2, C = 0.
boundary2(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 2, C = #count{C2 : input(_,C2,_)} - 1.

outside2(R,C) :- boundary2(R,C).
outside2(R2,C2) :- outside2(R1,C1), adj(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC, input(R2,C2,V), V != 2.

% ---- Cells that are outside colour 1 ----
boundary1(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 1, R = 0.
boundary1(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 1, R = #count{R2 : input(R2,_,_)} - 1.
boundary1(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 1, C = 0.
boundary1(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != 1, C = #count{C2 : input(_,C2,_)} - 1.

outside1(R,C) :- boundary1(R,C).
outside1(R2,C2) :- outside1(R1,C1), adj(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC, input(R2,C2,V), V != 1.

% ---- Output colours ----
% interior to a 5‑wall becomes 2 (but not a 5 itself)
output(R,C,2) :- not outside5(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 5.

% interior to a 2‑wall but not to a 5‑wall becomes 1
output(R,C,1) :- not outside2(R,C), outside5(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 2.

% interior to a 1‑wall but not to a 5‑ or 2‑wall becomes 0
output(R,C,0) :- not outside1(R,C), outside2(R,C), outside5(R,C), input(R,C,V), V != 1.

% cells that stay with their original colour (non‑zero, outside all walls)
output(R,C,V) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, outside5(R,C), outside2(R,C), outside1(R,C).

% cells with value 0 that are outside all walls stay 0
output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0), outside5(R,C), outside2(R,C), outside1(R,C).

min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4‑neighbour moves
:- delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Cells reachable from the boundary without crossing a wall of colour C
outside(C,R,Col) :- input(R,Col,V), V != C, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(C,R,Col) :- input(R,Col,V), V != C, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(C,R,Col) :- input(R,Col,V), V != C, min_col(Cmin), Col = Cmin.
outside(C,R,Col) :- input(R,Col,V), V != C, max_col(Cmax), Col = Cmax.
outside(C,R2,Col2) :- outside(C,R1,Col1), delta(DR,DC), R2 = R1+DR, Col2 = Col1+DC,
                     input(R2,Col2,V2), V2 != C.

% Cells that cannot reach the boundary without crossing a 5‑wall (they become 2)
inside5(R,Col) :- not outside(5,R,Col), input(R,Col,V), V != 5.

% Cells that cannot reach the boundary without crossing a 2‑wall (they become 1)
inside2(R,Col) :- not outside(2,R,Col), input(R,Col,V), V != 2.

% Cells that cannot reach the boundary without crossing a 1‑wall (they become 0)
inside1(R,Col) :- not outside(1,R,Col), input(R,Col,V), V != 1.

% Cells become 2 (interior to a 5‑wall)
output(R,Col,2) :- inside5(R,Col).

% Cells become 1 (interior to a 2‑wall but not interior to a 5‑wall)
output(R,Col,1) :- inside2(R,Col), not inside5(R,Col).

% Cells become 0 (interior to a 1‑wall but not interior to a 5‑ or 2‑wall)
output(R,Col,0) :- inside1(R,Col), not inside5(R,Col), not inside2(R,Col).

% Original colour for cells that are not interior to any higher wall
output(R,Col,V) :- input(R,Col,V), V != 0,
                    :- not inside5(R,Col), not inside2(R,Col), not inside1(R,Col).
</asp>
